transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... well, I hope I'm doing this right. It's just... I'm a secondary school teacher, and lately, I've been dealing with a bit of a silly problem. I didn't even really want to come in, to be honest, because I don't want to make a fuss or take up too much of your time. 

But... well, I just can't seem to shake this feeling that certain staff emails, and even the morning announcements at school, are actually... sort of... coded messages about me? I know how that sounds, I really do. My colleagues have been very sweet about it, and they gently show me that the emails were just sent to everyone on the general staff list. And I see that, of course I do. But the feeling just kind of lingers anyway. 

I'm sure it's probably just me overthinking things, or maybe just stress from the school term, right? I hope I'm explaining it okay... does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things in your life, not just the emails or announcements at school?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I mean... I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just this terribly anxious person, because I'm truly not. Outside of this... well, this silly business with the emails, everything else is quite lovely, really. 

I suppose I worry about the normal things, like whether my students are properly prepared for their exams or if I've graded things on time, but certainly nothing excessive. I really do try my best to handle things well and stay positive. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm making a fuss over every little thing in my life, because I usually cope quite well.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually self-conscious or fearful of being judged by others in social or work situations?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I don't come across as someone who is terribly insecure or anything like that. I actually quite enjoy my colleagues, and I love being in the classroom with my students. 

I don't feel afraid of being judged at all, really. I always try to be helpful and get along with everyone. It's really just... well, just that strange feeling about the emails, which I know is probably just me being silly. But in terms of just talking to people or doing my job, I feel quite comfortable. 

I hope that's helpful? I'm trying to be as clear as I can for you.
When you think the emails or announcements are coded messages about you, do you believe this in the sense that you feel certain it’s true, even though others say otherwise?

Um... well... I wouldn't say I'm *certain*, exactly. I mean, I don't want to sound completely unreasonable. I know my colleagues mean well when they point out the "To" line on the emails, and I do see that it says "All Staff." I really do try to be logical about it.

But... it's just... even when I look right at it, and even when they explain it so nicely, the feeling just doesn't go away. It still feels like... like there's a hidden meaning in the words, just for me. Like a little nudge or a hint that only I'm supposed to pick up on. 

I know it sounds a bit ridiculous when I say it out loud, and I'm so sorry if I'm not making much sense. I really do try to brush it off, I promise. It's just... hard to ignore when it feels so real in the moment. Am I explaining that okay? I hope I don't sound completely foolish.
Have you ever had experiences where you felt certain things were true, even when others couldn’t see it or agreed with you — things that weren’t related to the emails or announcements?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I really hope you don't think I'm just... losing my grip on reality everywhere else, because I'm truly not. It's really only ever been this one silly thing with the school emails and announcements. 

I try very hard to be sensible about everything else in my life, and I haven't noticed anything else feeling... well, off, or strange like that. I really am quite grounded usually, I promise. My husband and my friends, they've never had to correct me on anything else. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to reassure you that I'm not making a habit of imagining things all over the place. I really do try to be a very reasonable person.
Have you ever had any strong beliefs or suspicions that others don’t seem to share, even if you didn’t act on them or talk about them much?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I really try to keep a level head about most things. I don't want to come across as someone who is always suspicious or looking for trouble where there isn't any. I really do try to see the good in people and situations. 

It's... it's honestly just what I mentioned before. That's the whole reason I even made this appointment, actually. I just... I can't seem to shake this feeling that those staff emails and the morning announcements at school are... well, that they are really coded messages about me. 

Even when my colleagues are so sweet and gently show me that the emails were sent to the whole staff, or that the announcements are just general school business... I just still get that feeling. It's so embarrassing to admit, because I know it sounds a bit self-centered, and I really try not to be that kind of person. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for it. I'm just trying to be honest with you so you can help me understand why I might be feeling this way. Is that... does that answer your question alright?
Have you ever had any unusual thoughts or beliefs that others might find strange, even if you didn’t talk about them or act on them?

Oh dear, I feel terrible because I think I'm just giving you the exact same answer again. I'm so sorry if I'm not understanding the question properly, or if I'm being a bit repetitive. 

It truly is just... well, exactly what brought me in to see you today. Just that one strange feeling I can't seem to shake—that the morning announcements and the staff emails are actually coded messages about me. My colleagues are so wonderful and gently remind me that they're sent to everyone, but... the feeling just stays. 

I know most people would find that very strange, which is why I'm so embarrassed to keep bringing it up. I really don't have any other unusual thoughts besides that one silly thing, I promise. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever experienced any other unusual perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or having thoughts that felt like they weren't your own?

Oh... um. Well. Hearing voices, that sounds so... serious, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind or anything like that. I promise I'm still very capable and put-together. 

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest so you can help me... there is one little thing. It's really nothing major, just a bit of an auditory trick, I'm sure. Sometimes, when my house is perfectly quiet, or right after the classroom empties out at the end of the school day... I do hear a woman's voice. 

It's nothing scary at all, I assure you! She just... says my name, or makes a very short little comment about whatever I'm doing at that moment, like grading papers or organizing my desk. It's just that it sounds so normal and clear that I've actually answered her out loud a few times before I look up and realize there's no one else in the room with me. 

It's probably just my brain being so used to a noisy school environment all day, don't you think? Like an echo? I hope admitting that doesn't make me sound terrible or unhinged... I'm just really trying to give you all the right information. Is that... is that the sort of thing you meant?
When you hear the woman’s voice, is there ever any possibility that it could be coming from a real person nearby—like another room, a recording, or someone just outside the door?

Oh, I really wish I could say yes, because that would make so much more sense, wouldn't it? I always try to be very logical about it, I promise. Whenever it happens at school, I actually get up from my desk and peek out into the hallway, or check the next classroom over, just in case it's a colleague or one of the custodians working late. 

But... no, the halls are always completely empty. And at home, well, it's just me there. I even check to make sure I didn't leave the television or the radio on by accident, or that a window isn't open, because I really don't want to jump to any silly conclusions. But it's always just perfectly quiet when it happens. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too... abnormal. I really do look for a reasonable, everyday explanation first, because I want to be sensible about this. Did I answer that the way you needed?
When you hear the woman’s voice, are there any external sounds or people nearby that could be causing it, or does it seem to come from inside your mind?

Oh, dear, I hope I didn't confuse things with my last answer! Let me try to explain it a bit better. There really aren't any external noises or people causing it, but... it doesn't exactly *feel* like it's just inside my mind, either. That's the part that makes me feel so silly. 

It sounds completely external to me. When the woman's voice says my name, or makes that short little comment about what I'm doing, it is so clear that I actually answer out loud. I literally speak back to her before I look up and realize there is absolutely no one there. 

If it just felt like a thought inside my head, I don't think I would reply to it like that, you know? I only realize it *must* be coming from my mind after the fact, because the house or the classroom is perfectly quiet and empty. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful and answering your question properly.
Has the woman’s voice ever told you to do something or given you specific instructions that you felt you needed to follow?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that! I would definitely tell you if she did, but she's never... she's never bossy or demanding at all. I know how terrible that would sound, hearing voices telling you to do things. I promise you, it's nothing like that. 

Like I was saying before, it's really just... very brief, harmless things. Just in those quiet moments at home or when the school is empty. She might just say my name, or... or make a tiny little observation about whatever I'm doing right then, like grading or tidying up. Just a quick comment, clear enough that I might say "Yes?" or "Just finishing up" before I realize I'm alone. 

She never gives me instructions or tells me to do anything bad or strange. It's very mild, really. I hope that reassures you? I really don't want you to worry that I'm... well, a danger to myself or my students or anything awful like that. I'm still doing my job perfectly fine, I promise. Did that answer what you were looking for?
Have you ever experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs that you haven't mentioned yet, even if they seemed minor or fleeting?

Oh, um... well, I suppose there is one other little thing. I feel incredibly foolish even bringing it up, to be completely honest with you. I really want to be helpful and tell you everything, but I know how silly this is going to sound. 

Lately, I've just been having this... this strange feeling at school. It's about the general staff emails and the morning announcements over the PA system. Sometimes I just can't shake the feeling that they are actually... well, that they contain coded messages specifically directed at me. 

My colleagues are so wonderful, and when I've brought it up, they very gently show me the email addresses to prove the messages were sent to absolutely everyone on staff. And logically, I know they are right. I really do! But it's just this nagging feeling I can't quite turn off, even when they show me the proof. 

I hope you don't think I'm completely losing my grip on reality. I know it's an irrational thought, which is exactly why I came in to talk to someone about it. I'm trying very hard to keep things in perspective. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed something was real or true, even though others couldn’t see it or agreed with you, and it wasn’t related to the emails, announcements, or the voice you hear?

Oh, no... no, I really don't think so. I've been trying to think very carefully about all of this, because I want to make sure I'm giving you the complete picture. But honestly, aside from the emails and announcements... and that brief little voice we talked about... no, there hasn't been anything else. 

I really do try to stay very grounded. My life is mostly just my lesson plans and my quiet evenings at home, so there isn't much room for anything else strange to happen, thankfully. I hope it's alright that I don't have anything else to add for that one? I promise I'm not keeping anything from you, I just... I really haven't experienced anything else like that. 

Am I doing okay with all these questions? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that others don’t seem to share, even if you didn’t talk about them or act on them?

Oh, um... beliefs or suspicions? No, I really don't think so. I've been racking my brain trying to make sure I give you all the right answers, but... no, no secret suspicions or anything like that. 

I really try to see the best in people, and I'd hate for you to think I was, well, distrustful of everyone around me. I promise I'm not like that at all. The other teachers at school and my friends are just so lovely, I don't have any reason to suspect them of anything outside of that silly email thing we already talked about. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for you, and I'd hate to leave anything out if you needed it. Is it alright that my answer is no for this one? I'm trying my best to give you exactly what you need.
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that you knew were completely irrational, but you couldn't stop thinking about them, even if you didn't act on them?

Oh, goodness... um, let me think about that for just a moment. Irrational thoughts that I just couldn't stop... well, aside from what I already mentioned about the emails, which I know is silly... no, I really don't believe so. 

I feel a bit dreadful that I keep giving you all these 'no' answers! I promise I'm searching my memory because I truly want to be as helpful as possible for you. But my mind is usually just so busy with grading essays and setting up my classroom, I don't really find myself getting stuck on other thoughts like that. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything to report for that one? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions and giving you what you need.
Have you ever believed something was happening or true that you know most people would think is completely impossible or unrealistic?

Oh, impossible or unrealistic? Um... no, no, definitely not. I mean, I know the things with the emails and the announcements sound a bit much, and I'm so embarrassed to have even brought them up, but... no, nothing like aliens or, you know, magic or anything completely out there like that. 

I really try to keep my feet on the ground. As a teacher, you have to be practical, right? You have to deal with facts and schedules. So, no, I haven't had any beliefs like that. I really hope I'm not frustrating you by not having more to say. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. Am I... am I still being helpful? I just want to make sure we're on the right track.
Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something was happening that you know most people would say is not real, even if you didn’t talk about it or act on it?

Oh, um... something most people would say isn't real? Like... like a fantasy or a delusion? Oh, goodness, no. No, I haven't experienced anything like that. 

I feel terrible, I feel like I'm just repeating myself and wasting your time with all these 'no's. I really am trying to think deeply about your questions, I promise. But honestly, aside from getting a little overly stressed about school things, my mind is very... ordinary, I suppose. Just lesson plans and grading, really. 

I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of answers you're looking for. I'd hate to be a difficult patient when you're just trying to help me. Am I doing okay?
